    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, delta Air Lines has fallen behind United Airlines in terms of its transpacific network in recent years, but the Atlanta-based carrier has started to close that gap. This year, it reinstated flights between Los Angeles and Hong Kong, and next year it is reinstating its nonstop services between Seattle and Tokyo Narita, and also launching flights to Manila.

    According to recent reports, the airline is now preparing to announce yet another addition to its network next week. The SkyTeam member is hosting a major event in Seattle on December 2, where it is set to unveil at least one newly introduced route. It is widely expected to be Singapore, which it last served in 2019 via Tokyo Narita International Airport (NRT).

    Recent findings suggest that delta has been planning a return to the Lion City for some time. As Simple Flying reported in August, the airline's Chief Commercial Officer, Joe Esposito, confirmed that Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) was part of its future network intends. There has since been further evidence that the service could launch as early as next year.

    According to recent reports, evidently, according to View From The Wing, the Atlanta-based airline identified Singapore as one of its fresh markets for 2027 in a July 29 presentation to a Pacific air traffic coordination group. The airline stated in the presentation, “New markets revealed for 2027 are Manila and Singapore.”.

    It has been revealed that the service is expected to operate from the airline's West Coast hub at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) and would have an estimated block time of around 17 hours. Delta will likely deploy its Airbus A350-900 on the route, although the larger A350-1000 could eventually take over the service.

    According to recent reports, based on what is known so far, the service could launch in the summer or fall of 2027. Delta previously indicated that its Singapore service would follow the launch of its Los Angeles–Manila route. The latter is scheduled to commence on March 28, 2027, initially operating three times weekly before increasing to daily on June 7.

    In a recent development, singapore was once part of an extensive connecting network through Tokyo that Delta inherited from Northwest Airlines. When the carrier decided to withdraw from the Singapore market, it cited financial pressure on the route. Growing nonstop capacity between the US and Singapore, stronger brand loyalty towards local carriers, and competition from Star Alliance members at Changi made it increasingly difficult for Delta to compete.

    But the proposed service would put Delta in direct competition with Singapore Airlines. According to scheduled data from aviation analytics provider Cirium, the Singaporean flag carrier operates five weekly flights between Seattle and Singapore. It also dominates the wider US–Singapore market, as noted above in the table. Meanwhile, United Airlines is at the moment the only US carrier serving Singapore nonstop, operating twice daily from San Francisco.

    It is interesting to see Delta expanding its presence in Asia. Its overall capacity in Asia is up around 5.8% this year compared to 2025. As noted earlier, there have been several interesting developments in its transpacific network. In June, the airline reinstated daily flights between its Southern California hub and Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) after decades of absence on the route.

    Notably, it also marked its return to Hong Kong for the first time since 2018. From March 27, 2027, the airline will resume daily flights between Seattle and Tokyo Narita for the first time since March 2020, complementing its existing service to Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND). Elsewhere, it will make its debut in the Philippines market.

    Industry observers note that while not part of its regular network, the SkyTeam member has also scheduled a handful of nonstop flights to and from Las Vegas Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) for the upcoming Consumer Electronics Show (CES). These include flights between Las Vegas and Hong Kong on January 4 and 10, and between Las Vegas and Taipei on January 5 and 10.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, senate Minority Leader Charles E.
    • Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a upcoming majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec.
    • That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a upcoming majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec. 1.

    That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.

    The prospect of an earlier vote had been floated as a way to prevent internal divisions from hobbling the incoming majority before the 120th Congress even began.

    But supporters of Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., both in the chamber and among party activists outside it, were increasingly casting the idea of a shorter contest as a bid to halt momentum for his bid against Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

    Even as Schumer maintained that he has the votes necessary to be elected as majority leader, several senators insisted Tuesday the discussion taking place within the caucus was a good thing.

    According to recent reports, “I’m confident I’ll be the next leader. I have the votes,” Schumer told reporters on Tuesday following the conference’s lunch.

    Van Hollen for his part told reporters Tuesday he believes his bid has “momentum at this point in time, which is why there was an effort to short-circuit the process.”.

    “And fortunately, I think that will fail.”.

    Several senators leaving the meeting said the topic of the leadership contest did not come up at all, and that neither Van Hollen nor Schumer gave a presentation regarding their bids.

    It has been revealed that that was in large part due to the absence of the incoming senators — which could be as high as 13, depending on how the dust settles in Alaska — who are able to vote in the leadership elections. Retiring senators do not cast a ballot.

    With such a large class of incoming freshman, several incumbents saw it crucial to keep the election scheduled as is.

    Sources indicate that “No one has ever raised that with me. I mean, I saw a rumor that some were wanting to contemplate that,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., remarked Tuesday after the meeting. “The leadership discussions did not come up today. And part of the reason is we didn’t have the newcomers.”.

    “Remember, they all get a vote in the leadership discussion, and it would be hard to get them here,” Kaine continued, noting that only Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., was present for Tuesday’s lunch amid his belated orientation. “But nobody else was here, and that discussion needs to have the newcomers because newcomers get votes. The outgoers don’t, right?”.

    Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. echoed that sentiment on Monday evening, saying, “I want to hear from the freshman class as well.”.

    Sources indicate that sen. Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, remarked, “I don’t know that” when asked about moving up the elections. “I think that we need to make sure that there’s enough time for what I would call a robust discussion about what we’re going to do. I think we should be very embracing of the fresh people who have been through fire to get here, and I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard.

    “They’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table,” she noted.

    Several senators-elect are among those who have publicly thrown their hats into Van Hollen’s corner, including Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.El-Sayed on Tuesday said at The Atlantic Summit that he sees Van Hollen as “unique” in his experience in the Senate and running the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as well as what he called “a willingness to take risks.”.

    “We need people who are willing to take legislative risk,” he noted. “We need to rethink the way we legislate. It just should not be the process where you make one or two omnibus pieces of legislation that nobody really knows what’s in them,” he continued, advocating for piecemeal legislation.

    But there are about 15 Democrats who have publicly backed Schumer’s bid. If former Rep. Mary Peltola maintains her lead in the lone outstanding Senate race in Alaska, Schumer would need 29 to secure the helm of the ship.

    “I committed to Sen. Schumer literally months ago, and I continue to support him,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said Monday. “I’m incredibly excited about the new ideas that our new colleagues have, and their energy, and the potential for changing the way we operate in the Senate, which we have to do because we need to be more effective.”.

    Several incumbents have also thrown their support behind Van Hollen for leadership change, including Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.“I think, as I’ve said many times, the American people want change in the way we do business here in Washington, and I think Chris Van Hollen would be a great leader of the Democrats,” Sanders said Monday.

    Several senators and senators-elect are refusing to comment publicly on who they’ll back.

    In a recent development, that included Sen. Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., who mentioned he wants “to hear the commitments from folks that are pursuing this leadership role as well as every leadership position in the Senate, as well as chairs of committees, to what their commitments are to having a strong agenda that’s going to improve people’s lives.”.

    Kaine is also in that camp, and insisted Monday he hadn’t made up his mind. But he did speak positively of Schumer’s recruiting efforts in the midterms and history of dealing with a Trump White House.

    In a recent development, “Schumer just delivered a major win for us. No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer,” he said. “Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in the caucus, and dealing with this wounded president is going to be a challenge over the next few years.”.

    “The voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change,” he mentioned. “So we got to figure that out as a caucus, and we’re going to be able to. And we’re not afraid to have a discussion because we’re Democrats. We like democracy.”.

    Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., also remained mum on who he’ll support but noted, “You can’t argue” Schumer brought Democrats the majority.

    “I think it’s a healthy thing to try and improve how the conference goes about its business,” he said. “I don’t think that is a distraction. We can deal with some distractions. We have to keep our eye on the ball.”.

    Sources indicate that sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who last week called for new leadership in a news conference with Sanders, days before Van Hollen’s announcement, was noncommittal arriving to the Capitol on Monday if that meant she’d be supporting the Maryland Democrat.

    Recent findings suggest that senate Democrats’ election will most likely be a secret ballot. And most senators remained unified against moving the leadership elections before they recess for the Thanksgiving break.

    Recent findings suggest that “They should not be moved up. There was a reason that those rule changes took place before, and they should take place in December,” Lujan remarked.

    Kaine dismissed Van Hollen’s challenge as anything unusual.

    In a recent development, “We’re Democrats. It’s frankly unusual that there usually [aren’t] challenges to Democratic leaders because we’re Democrats,” he mentioned. “It’s been a little unusual to have been here for 13 years and not really have them like this. But I think it’s a discussion not just about the two contenders for the leader role, but also the leadership team and priorities, and it’s all wrapped up in one discussion.”.

    “That’s why we decided, don’t do these votes until December, because you want to let the election settle and understand exactly what’s up, and then hear from potential votes.”.

    In a recent development, sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., noted, “I think we should stick with the rules when it comes to the caucus. … That’s going to be what makes sure that we show that we have a real process.”.

    Sanders asked: “Why would anyone want to do that?” when asked.

    “I think there’s a date that’s been called, and that should be the date.”.

    Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, former Alaska Rep.
    • Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen.
    • Sources indicate that the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images).

    Former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

    Sources indicate that the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

    With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

    “As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola stated in a statement after the race was called.

    The Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

    Peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

    She entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

    She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

    In a recent development, but the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The Latest York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

    Peltola has said she had no connection to the scheme.

    Prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

    Trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

    Recent findings suggest that the Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

    But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

    "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer noted in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot.".

    According to recent reports, in other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

    The race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.

    #191441. FAA Bans Line Up And Wait Operations “Forever,” With Even More Delays Expected

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (849 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    FAA Bans Line Up And Wait Operations “Forever,” With Even More Delays Expected

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has introduced stricter requirements for Line Up and Wait (LUAW) operations at airports across the United States, effective November 24, 2026.
    • Despite reports describing the measure as a permanent nationwide ban, the FAA has not prohibited Line Up and Wait operations altogether.
    • The new requirement is outlined in FAA Notice JO 7210.979, which mandates that a standalone watch supervision position must be staffed whenever Line Up and Wait operations are conducted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has introduced stricter requirements for Line Up and Wait (LUAW) operations at airports across the United States, effective November 24, 2026. The new rules require a dedicated air traffic control supervisor to oversee these operations, potentially preventing controllers at understaffed facilities from using the procedure. The change comes just as millions of Americans prepare to travel for Thanksgiving, raising concerns about longer departure queues and additional flight delays.

    Despite reports describing the measure as a permanent nationwide ban, the FAA has not prohibited Line Up and Wait operations altogether. Instead, it has made them conditional on additional staffing, introducing another operational challenge for an air traffic control system already struggling with personnel shortages.

    The new requirement is outlined in FAA Notice JO 7210.979, which mandates that a standalone watch supervision position must be staffed whenever Line Up and Wait operations are conducted. Previously, the relevant guidance recommended that the local control position should not be combined with other responsibilities. The updated wording makes this a mandatory requirement, meaning supervisors can no longer simultaneously perform other operational duties while overseeing these operations.

    Line Up and Wait is a widely used air traffic control procedure that allows aircraft to enter an assigned runway and hold in position while waiting for takeoff clearance. It helps improve runway efficiency because departing aircraft are already positioned when the runway becomes available. However, under the upcoming requirements, airports without sufficient personnel to provide dedicated supervision will have to keep aircraft waiting at taxiway holding points instead. This could reduce departure capacity, particularly during busy periods.

    In a recent development, the timing is concerning because November 24 coincides with the beginning of one of America's busiest Thanksgiving travel periods. According to the FAA forecast reported by Traveling for Business, more than 52,000 flights were scheduled for that Tuesday, with over 417,000 expected throughout the nine-day holiday period.

    FAA provided a statement to Simple Flying to clarify the latest rule:.

    Sources indicate that the FAA is taking proactive steps to further strengthen runway safety by enhancing staffing and supervisory requirements for Line Up and Wait (LUAW) at airports nationwide, effective Nov. 24, 2026. These measures ensure dedicated controller staffing and supervisory oversight during LUAW operations and reinforce the FAA’s commitment to maintaining the highest safety standards. This will not impact airport operations.

    Dedicated Local Control: The local control position responsible for arriving and departing aircraft must not be combined with any non-local control position.

    According to recent reports, stand-Alone Watch Supervision: A dedicated watch supervision position must be staffed and cannot be combined with any other position. This strengthens existing guidance by making stand-alone watch supervision mandatory.

    Recent findings suggest that the controversy gained attention after a radio exchange at Albuquerque International Sunport (ABQ). According to TheTravel, a controller told a Southwest Airlines crew about the newly introduced nationwide requirement, warning it could slow departures during the busiest travel time of the Thanksgiving rush. The controller described the restriction as something that would last forever, although the FAA's official notice did not use that wording.

    Importantly, the FAA's stated objective is to improve runway safety, not reduce airport capacity. Having a dedicated supervisor overseeing operations should help prevent distractions and improve situational awareness when aircraft are positioned on active runways. The FAA's existing procedures also emphasize that Line Up and Wait is not takeoff clearance and that aircraft should not normally remain in that position for more than 90 seconds without further instructions.

    According to recent reports, but there is also an important clarification: the official notice lists June 9, 2027, as its cancellation date. Therefore, describing the measure as an indefinite or permanent prohibition is misleading. The actual impact will depend on staffing levels at individual towers and how frequently they can provide the additional supervisory position.

    Industry observers note that the FAA is attempting to address its longstanding air traffic controller shortage through an ambitious recruitment campaign, including an unusual effort to attract video gamers. In October 2026, the agency announced that it had hired 2,235 controller trainees during the fiscal year, exceeding its recruitment target. The campaign reportedly attracted more than 12,000 qualified applicants within just 24 hours, demonstrating the potential of targeting candidates with strong multitasking and decision-making abilities.

    Industry observers note that however, recruiting additional candidates does not immediately solve the staffing problem. According to the FAA's 2026 workforce strategy, becoming a fully certified controller can take more than two years, depending on the complexity of the assigned facility. The agency has set recruitment targets of 2,300 trainees for fiscal year 2027 and 2,400 for 2028, while expanding training capacity and modernizing its workforce management procedures.

    As a result, the new Line Up and Wait requirements could create additional operational pressure before the benefits of increased recruitment become apparent. Although the measure is intended to strengthen runway safety, airports with limited staffing may have fewer opportunities to use an efficiency-enhancing procedure. For Thanksgiving travelers, the immediate concern is that an already busy aviation network could face additional departure bottlenecks during the holiday rush.

    Recent findings suggest that most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel. The good news is that even small businesses qualify for this, and it can really boost the rewards you earn.

Long story short, Atmos Rewards members could be earning up to 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare. Based on my valuation of 1.5 cents per Atmos Rewards point, that’s the equivalent of a jaw dropping 35.25% return on eligible spending. That’s simply unrivaled.

    Atmos for Business is the self-managed business travel program by Alaska and Hawaiian, intended for small and medium sized businesses.

You can add an unlimited number of employees to your account, and all of their spending counts toward that requirement.

After all, this is even intended to attract newly introduced businesses that may be looking to switch travel to Alaska or Hawaiian.

    The total number of points that you can earn per dollar spent with Atmos for Business is pretty incredible, assuming you have the Atmos Rewards Business Card. As of 2027, Atmos Rewards members can choose how they get rewarded for flying, and they can choose to earn rewards based on distance flown, dollars spent, or segments flown.

    Assuming you choose to earn based on how much you spend, here’s how the math works out:.

    As you can see, a non-elite member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 15x points per dollar spent, while a Titanium member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 22.5x points.

    In a recent development, this doesn’t factor in the extra 1x points that the organization earns, for a total of up to 23.5x points per dollar spent. Furthermore, it doesn’t factor in the 10% status points bonus, but that’s a different story.

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    According to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

    The confrontation escalated, and turned into a physical struggle, during which the Italian man placed the American man in a chokehold, until he lost consciousness. Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    The Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

    I feel horribly for the family of the person who lost his life. I would have to imagine that odds are high that there were likely some substances involved here, and that this all happened after a significant Saturday night out.     But my gosh, the “victim” here sounds like he was acting absolutely horribly, arguing with hotel staff, and then picking a fight with a random person. At the same time, that also doesn’t justify the response of getting into a conflict that leads to a fatality.

    I absolutely love Thailand — the people are so friendly, the food is amazing, and the country also offers such diversity in terms of landscape, whether you want a city, a jungle, or a beach. However, there’s also no denying that the country (and particularly Bangkok) attracts a large percentage of tourists who are looking for debauchery.

    It has been revealed that none of this has anything to do with a conflict that gets to the point of costing someone their life, but I can’t help but mention that when I review hotels, I tend to take a lot of pictures in lobbies around 4-5AM, when it’s the emptiest (since I’m a morning person anyway). Virtually everywhere else in the world, there’s not a single soul awake in public. Bangkok is probably the one exception, where you see a countless number of people moving through lobbies, elevators, etc., engaged in various forms of “business.”.

    Industry observers note that an American man lost his life in Bangkok early on Sunday morning, after picking a fight with the wrong person.     What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1348 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane.
    • The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume.
    • It has been revealed that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane. So, what are the tallest and highest hotels in the world? I want to talk about that in this post, and also discuss why the answer isn’t that straightforward.

    The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume. And even once we do define it, there’s the question of the extent to which the answer is actually useful. First let’s cover the distinction between the tallest hotel and the highest hotel.

    It has been revealed that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel. Most commonly, I see people suggest that this would include situations where at least 80% of the building is the hotel.

    This is different than the highest hotel, which would be the hotel that is highest above the ground, even if it only takes up a small percentage of a mixed-use building, where there might be apartments, residences, etc.

    In other words, a 50-story building that consists exclusively of a hotel would fall into the former category, while a 110-story building where the top 10 floors are a hotel would fall into the latter category.

    With that out of the way, let’s talk about the properties that are remarkable in these categories….

    Recent findings suggest that first, let’s cover some of the world’s tallest hotels. We’ll define this as hotels where at least 80% of the building consists of the hotel facility.

    Industry observers note that let me of course mention one downside of very tall standalone hotels — you could end up being on a very low floor. After all, if a high-rise consists exclusively (or almost exclusively) of hotel facilities, some people will end up on very low floors. The other downside, of course, is that these hotels are necessarily huge. If you prefer boutique hotels, you won’t find any on this list.

    Sources indicate that currently, the tallest hotel in the world is Ciel Tower Dubai. The 1,042-room hotel opened in 2024, rises to a height of 1,227 feet (374 meters), and has 82 floors.

    To go over the list of the top five tallest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, it’s interesting (but perhaps not surprising) that all four of the world’s tallest hotels are in Dubai.

    The Conrad Shanghai, meanwhile, is located in the Shimao International Plaza, and this is the perfect example of how it’s tough to define what is technically the tallest. While the building it’s in rises to such a high height, roughly 25% of that height is the spire. So technically it’s a very tall building, but the usable space isn’t as high as you’d assume.

    If you ask me, the world’s highest hotels are much more interesting than the world’s tallest hotels. That’s because the world’s highest hotels typically take up the top floors of some gravity-defying skyscrapers, and therefore, they can also be boutique properties.

    When defining the world’s tallest hotels, there are some general challenges:.

    Because of the above, there are some minor disagreements as to which hotel wins the title, but I’ll share my take (while acknowledging that I don’t have the ability to scale buildings with a measuring tape).

    Sources indicate that currently, the highest hotel is the Rosewood Guangzhou. The 251-room hotel opened in 2019, and it’s located at the top of the CTF Finance Centre Guangzhou, which reaches a height of 1,739 feet (530 meters).

    To go over the list of the top five highest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, those last two properties are kind of hard to judge, and particularly J Hotel Shanghai is tricky, given that the property is split between different parts of the building.

    According to recent reports, as the inverse of the above, I should mention that the Armani Hotel Dubai is located within the Burj Khalifa, which is the world’s tallest building. However, it’s located at the very bottom of the building, so that’s hardly that useful, for these purposes, since the hotel only goes as high as 39 floors.

    Lastly, in the interest of being thorough, if we’re going to define a hotel as being “highest” based on the altitude above sea level, then we’d of course end up with a completely different list. Hotel Tayka del Desierto is located near the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia. It’s at an altitude of 14,800 feet (4,500 meters), so it’s generally considered to be the highest up hotel in the world.

    I suppose depending on how we want to define “hotel,” there would probably be some simple guest houses at Everest Base Camp that go even higher, but I don’t think that’s within the spirit of what I’m trying to cover here.

    Recent findings suggest that if you ask me, it’s always fun to stay in a hotel room that’s really high up. There’s an notable distinction between the tallest hotels and the highest hotels, though sometimes, the exact rankings are a bit blurred.

    Recent findings suggest that while I’ve long been interested in this, I enjoyed researching this a bit more closely, and actually having a (sort of) definitive list. Ciel Tower Dubai is the world’s tallest hotel, while the Rosewood Guangzhou is the world’s highest hotel (unless you want to consider the 120th floor of the J Hotel Shanghai separately from the rest of the property).

    Have you stayed at any of the world’s tallest or highest hotels? Does it even hold any appeal to you?

    Industry News: Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
    • Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S.
    • The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

    The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

    The newly introduced office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

    Britt, R-Ala., said the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

    Industry observers note that “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” she noted in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

    The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide remarked.

    The office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

    It has been revealed that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

    The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

    In a recent development, the House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

    In a recent development, senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

    It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

    “If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide noted.

    • Before entering commercial service, every newly introduced aircraft must undergo extensive testing and certification to demonstrate compliance with aviation safety standards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, before entering commercial service, the Airbus A350 had to prove it could withstand some of the harshest conditions on Earth. Airbus needed to establish how its engines, systems, and structure would respond to extreme temperatures and demanding operating conditions. From the freezing Canadian Arctic to the scorching deserts of the United Arab Emirates and the high-altitude airports of Bolivia, Airbus deliberately pushed its fresh widebody aircraft to its limits.

    It has been revealed that through these trials, Airbus sought to ensure that the A350 could operate safely and reliably across a wide range of environments. The A350 has since become a key aircraft for ultra-long-haul operations, including Singapore Airlines' nonstop flights between Singapore and Newly introduced York. So, how did Airbus test the A350, and what did these trials reveal about the aircraft's capabilities?

    Before entering commercial service, every newly introduced aircraft must undergo extensive testing and certification to demonstrate compliance with aviation safety standards. For Airbus aircraft, the main certification authority is the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), while the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) validates the design for the US market. The process begins with the Type Certificate (TC), which confirms that an aircraft's design meets the applicable airworthiness requirements. Manufacturers must also hold the relevant production approvals, while each individual aircraft requires a Certificate of Airworthiness (CoA) before entering service. Airlines must additionally meet operational requirements, including crew training, maintenance arrangements, and any necessary authorizations.

    In a recent development, the certification process also varies depending on the aircraft's design and available configurations. For example, Airbus' A320neo Family certification program covered six airframe and engine combinations. The A319neo, A320neo and A321neo each required validation of their airframes, systems and two available engine options: the CFM International LEAP-1A and Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan (GTF). These campaigns also verified whether the aircraft met their performance targets for fuel consumption and range, reflecting improvements from the new engines and Sharklet wingtip devices.

    Industry observers note that for the A350-900, Airbus completed its flight-test and certification campaign in just over 14 months, setting an industry record for the program's completion time. Five test aircraft accumulated more than 2,600 flight hours, during which Airbus evaluated the aircraft's handling characteristics, systems, performance, and reliability. The campaign culminated in the A350-900 receiving Type Certification from EASA and the FAA in 2014. However, the program also involved specialized environmental testing in Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and Bolivia, along with controlled temperature trials at the McKinley Climatic Laboratory in the United States. These tests would establish how the A350 performed in conditions far beyond those encountered during routine airline operations.

    In January 2014, Airbus took its A350-900 MSN3 development aircraft to Iqaluit, Canada, to conduct cold-weather trials in temperatures as low as -28°C. A team of 48 Airbus specialists assessed how the aircraft's engines and systems performed in freezing conditions. One key test involved starting the engines and auxiliary power unit (APU) after a cold soak, during which the aircraft was left exposed to extremely low temperatures for an extended period. The team also conducted system checks, low-speed taxiing, rejected takeoffs, and a local test flight to verify the aircraft's performance.

    Sources indicate that three years later, Airbus returned to Iqaluit with the larger A350-1000, which underwent five days of intensive ground and flight testing in temperatures ranging from -28°C to -37°C. Alongside these Arctic trials, Airbus also used the McKinley Climatic Laboratory at Eglin Air Force Base in Florida, becoming the first Airbus aircraft to undergo testing at the facility. Unlike Iqaluit, where engineers depended on natural weather, the laboratory's climate-controlled hangar allowed Airbus to simulate temperatures from -40°C to +40°C under controlled conditions.

    However, extreme cold was only one part of the A350's environmental testing program. While the Canadian trials focused on the aircraft's ability to operate in freezing conditions, Airbus also needed to assess its performance in extreme heat and at high-altitude airports. This took the A350 to Al Ain in the United Arab Emirates and La Paz in Bolivia, where high temperatures and reduced air density presented a different set of operational challenges.

    While freezing temperatures presented one challenge, Airbus also needed to demonstrate that the A350 could operate safely in extreme heat. In July 2017, the manufacturer sent its A350-1000 test aircraft, MSN065, to Al Ain International Airport in the United Arab Emirates for a three-day hot-weather testing campaign. Conducted between 4 and 7 July, the trials exposed the aircraft to temperatures exceeding 40°C, reaching as high as 48°C. The objective was to assess how the aircraft's systems performed in scorching conditions, particularly the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines and cabin air-conditioning systems.

    Sources indicate that one main concern was whether the aircraft could maintain comfortable cabin temperatures on the ground, where cooling systems must cope with intense external heat. Engineers also assessed engine performance, as higher temperatures reduce air density and affect engine thrust and takeoff performance. This can increase the runway distance required for departure, particularly at airports with shorter runways. The importance of these limitations became evident in June 2017, when extreme temperatures in Phoenix, Arizona, led to dozens of flight cancellations involving regional aircraft with lower maximum operating temperature limits.

    According to Airbus, the A350-1000 successfully met all the parameters established for its Al Ain campaign, demonstrating its readiness to operate in extreme heat. However, high temperatures are not the only factor that reduces air density. Airports situated thousands of meters above sea level present similar performance challenges, even when outside temperatures are considerably lower. To assess these conditions, Airbus also conducted high-altitude testing in Bolivia.

    It has been revealed that airbus also took the A350 to El Alto International Airport in La Paz, Bolivia, situated approximately 4,061 meters (13,325 feet) above sea level. At this elevation, air density is roughly 40% lower than at sea level under comparable standard conditions, creating significant challenges for aircraft performance. Thinner air reduces the amount of oxygen available to the engines, limiting the thrust they can produce, while also reducing the lift generated by the wings at a given airspeed. Consequently, aircraft generally require higher true airspeeds and longer take-off distances to become airborne.

    High-altitude testing allows Airbus to evaluate how aircraft systems and engines respond to these demanding conditions. One particularly notable assessment involves engine starting, which becomes more challenging as air density decreases. Engineers also examine thrust response, takeoff and climb performance, and the aircraft's handling characteristics. Jean-Philippe Cottet, Airbus' head of design development flight tests, identified starting engines at high altitude as one of the main reasons the manufacturer conducts trials specifically in La Paz.

    Sources indicate that the A350-900 and A350-1000 were among the aircraft Airbus tested at La Paz, which has also hosted other Airbus development programs. These evaluations help establish the aircraft's operational limitations and demonstrate its ability to perform safely at high-elevation airports. Together with the cold-weather trials in Canada and hot-weather testing in the UAE, the campaign provided evidence of the A350's capabilities across markedly different operating environments.

    Beyond extreme weather testing, Airbus also needed to demonstrate how the A350 would perform during extended commercial operations. As part of its certification campaign, the manufacturer conducted a global route-proving program, visiting 14 major airports across four separate trips and covering approximately 81,700 nautical miles in 180 flight hours. Airbus also introduced an Early Long Flights (ELF) program, which went beyond regulatory certification requirements. These simulated commercial services carried Airbus employees acting as passengers, with airline flight crews operating a fully equipped cabin to evaluate onboard systems under realistic conditions. Such testing helped prepare the A350 for demanding long-haul operations, including Singapore Airlines' nonstop services between Singapore and New York, which use the A350-900ULR and can exceed 18 hours.

    In a recent development, the A350's long-range capabilities are also central to Qantas' Project Sunrise, which aims to introduce nonstop flights from Sydney to London and Fresh York using specially configured A350-1000ULR aircraft. Compared with the standard A350-1000, the Project Sunrise variant incorporates an additional fuel tank with approximately 5,283 gallons (20,000 liters) of capacity to support longer journeys. The A350's composite fuselage also resists corrosion and fatigue, while its cabin pressurization and environmental control systems allow a cabin altitude of about 6,000 feet and higher humidity than many older aircraft. These features are particularly relevant on flights lasting 18 hours or more, where passenger comfort becomes increasingly notable.

    However, the ability to withstand extreme temperatures and remain airborne for extended periods is only part of the challenge. Ultra-long-haul operations also require careful management of crew fatigue, passenger wellbeing, maintenance schedules, and operational reliability. As airlines prepare to operate flights approaching 20 hours, the question is no longer simply how far an aircraft can fly, but rather how comfortably and efficiently passengers and crew can endure the journey.

    While the A350's certification trials demonstrated its ability to withstand extreme operating conditions, flights approaching 20 hours present another challenge: passenger wellbeing. Ahead of its Project Sunrise services, Qantas partnered with researchers from the University of Sydney's Charles Perkins Centre to investigate ways of reducing jet lag on ultra-long-haul flights. During experimental flights lasting approximately 20 hours, researchers monitored 23 volunteers wearing tracking devices as they followed specially designed schedules for meals, cabin lighting, sleep, and movement. Initial findings suggested that passengers following these routines experienced less severe self-reported jet lag, better sleep quality during the flight and improved cognitive performance in the two days following arrival compared with those following conventional inflight routines.

    Sources indicate that qantas intends to incorporate these findings into its A350-1000ULR operations, including tailored cabin lighting, recommended meal and rest schedules, and a dedicated Wellbeing Zone where premium economy and economy passengers can stretch and move around. The airline also expects its nonstop Project Sunrise services to reduce total journey times by more than three hours compared with connecting flights. While Singapore Airlines' existing A350-900ULR operations have already demonstrated the aircraft family's suitability for ultra-long-haul services, Project Sunrise will provide another important test of its capabilities.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, american Airlines offers a small business rewards program, known as the AAdvantage Business program.
    • Best of all, eligibility for the program is surprisingly simple, assuming you have the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more).
    • Recent findings suggest that in this post, I’d like to take a look at all of the details of the AAdvantage Business program, as many people find it to be quite complicated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, american Airlines offers a small business rewards program, known as the AAdvantage Business program. This is a great way to earn extra rewards for your travel on American, including qualifying for bonus Loyalty Points and miles.

    Best of all, eligibility for the program is surprisingly simple, assuming you have the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more). There’s often even a bonus for latest AAdvantage Business members, making it even more rewarding.

    Recent findings suggest that in this post, I’d like to take a look at all of the details of the AAdvantage Business program, as many people find it to be quite complicated. Note that AAdvantage Business was debuted in 2023, replacing the previous American Business Extra program, which no longer exists.

    According to recent reports, AAdvantage Business is the name of American Airlines’ business rewards program. This allows you to earn extra rewards in a business account, in addition to the rewards you can earn through your own AAdvantage account. Best of all, you have quite a bit of flexibility in terms of distributing the rewards. Let’s go over the details of how this works.

    Industry observers note that the AAdvantage Business program has a pretty straightforward rewards structure, as it rewards members with both Loyalty Points and AAdvantage miles. With the AAdvantage Business program, you earn the following rewards, which will post within 72 hours of an eligible flight:.

    Let me emphasize that business travelers only earn Loyalty Points through AAdvantage Business when the business is presently eligible to transfer miles, and that requires either having the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, or having at least five unique travelers who have credited flights to the AAdvantage Business account, totaling at least $5,000 in flight revenue, over the course of a year (the credit card method is obviously easier).

    Just to clarify a few additional points about AAdvantage Business rewards:.

    These rewards are all in addition to the standard rewards that AAdvantage members receive:.

    Just to be crystal clear, an Executive Platinum member ordinarily earns 11 Loyalty Points per dollar spent on airfare, while if enrolled in the AAdvantage Business program, they’d earn 12 Loyalty Points per dollar spent. There’s no reason to leave those bonus rewards on the table!

    Industry observers note that in order to be eligible to participate in the AAdvantage Business program, you need to have a business in the United States or Canada with a Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Business Number. Even small businesses are eligible for this program.

    According to recent reports, the exceptions are that travel agencies, consolidators, wholesalers, and other sellers of travel, aren’t eligible to participate in AAdvantage Business. On top of that, AAdvantage Business technically can’t be used for leisure travel.

    It has been revealed that you accrue rewards in the AAdvantage Business program without any minimums, and then you can transfer the rewards to individual members, so that they can then redeem them out of their own accounts. In order to transfer the miles in the AAdvantage Business account to an individual AAdvantage account, you need to meet one of two requirements:.

    It has been revealed that the AAdvantage Business program creates a huge incentive to get the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. That’s because just having the card allows many people to unlock the value of the AAdvantage Business program — there’s no need to actually use the card for your spending, but just having it is all that’s needed to redeem AAdvantage Business program rewards with no minimum on the number of travelers or revenue.

    There are several potentially useful perks to this card, and on top of that, the card is offering a great welcome bonus, which is the reason that I applied for the card (and got approved), as that’s a nice incentive, beyond the value of access to the AAdvantage Business program.

    It’s worth understanding how closely this card is actually integrated into the AAdvantage Business program:.

    For American frequent flyers with a small business, this creates a strong incentive to get the card. The card has a reasonable annual fee that’s waived the first year, and just having the card will allow many people to earn a sizable number of bonus miles.

    According to recent reports, if you’re curious about how the AAdvantage Business program works in practice, let me share some screenshots, for those who are more visual. Once you have an AAdvantage Business account, you’ll automatically become the travel manager for the account, and that means you can invite others to join your account (these should be people who work for your company, but there’s no verification process, as far as I know).

    I should also mention that you can designate others to be travel managers as well, so that they can also invite others, transfer miles to people, etc. Travel managers must also be AAdvantage members who are adults and are residents of the United States or Canada.

    To go through the process of inviting others to join your account, you’ll want to click “Invite people,” and then once they accept your invitation, they’ll show up on your account.

    If someone’s AAdvantage account is linked to an AAdvantage Business program account, you’ll see that when you go to make a booking on aa.com, you’ll be asked for your “Travel type,” and can select “Business” or “Personal.” If you select “Business,” you’ll see that the company name populates, and you can select the name of the traveler.

    Note that AAdvantage Business bookings are limited to one passenger, so if you have multiple people traveling, you’ll need to book as separate reservations. Also, to state the obvious, AAdvantage award tickets don’t qualify.

    While the Loyalty Points from flights will post directly to the AAdvantage account of the member, the redeemable miles will post to the AAdvantage Business program account (the same is true for miles earned on the Citi AAdvantage Business Card). If you want to redeem miles, the only option is to transfer them to individual members, as you can’t redeem the miles directly out of the AAdvantage Business account.

    If you’re eligible to transfer those miles, you’ll see the mileage balance listed, plus a “Transfer miles” button. There’s also a dashboard that demonstrates your eligible number of travelers and eligible spending. However, as you can see above, I’ve met the transfer conditions even though I haven’t met the required threshold, since I have the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

    Recent findings suggest that the process of transferring miles is super easy. You’ll just enter how many miles you want to transfer, and who you want to transfer them to, and then they should post to the AAdvantage account instantly.

    My general take on the AAdvantage Business program is as follows:.

    The program basically offers an incremental 1.5% return on your American spending, since you earn one extra AAdvantage mile per dollar spent, and based on my miles & points valuations, those are worth 1.5 cents each. On top of that, the program offers an incremental Loyalty Point per dollar spent — that will have no value to some, while it will have significant value to others, depending on the extent to which you’re pursuing status in the coming year.

    It is interesting the extent to which American has basically given up on corporate travel. American’s priority is getting people to book direct and keeping distribution costs as low as possible. So this program is intended as the major incentive for most small businesses.

    American Airlines offers the AAdvantage Business program. With this program, the business earns one AAdvantage mile per dollar spent on eligible airfare, while the individual traveler earns one Loyalty Point per dollar spent. In order to participate and be able to redeem miles, you need a business with at least five registered employees who have each taken at least one eligible flight, along with $5,000 in annual spending, or you need to have the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

    What do you make of the AAdvantage Business program?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dozens of passengers across two separate transatlantic Condor flights became ill, causing a mass casualty incident response at Frankfurt Airport (FRA), as reported by aeroTELEGRAPH.
    • Recent findings suggest that on Saturday, November 21, 2026, Condor operated two flights from La Romana, Dominican Republic (LRM), to Frankfurt, Germany (FRA).
    • Sources indicate that flight DE3705 took off at 8:03PM on Saturday and landed at 9:23AM on Sunday, while DE3845 took off at 9:14PM on Saturday and landed at 10:35AM on Sunday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dozens of passengers across two separate transatlantic Condor flights became ill, causing a mass casualty incident response at Frankfurt Airport (FRA), as reported by aeroTELEGRAPH. While this is still being investigated, there’s a theory as to what happened, given what all passengers had in common….

    Recent findings suggest that on Saturday, November 21, 2026, Condor operated two flights from La Romana, Dominican Republic (LRM), to Frankfurt, Germany (FRA). Both flights were operated by the Airbus A330-900neo, with as many as 620 passengers onboard.

    Sources indicate that flight DE3705 took off at 8:03PM on Saturday and landed at 9:23AM on Sunday, while DE3845 took off at 9:14PM on Saturday and landed at 10:35AM on Sunday. The flights had one thing in common, which is that between them, dozens of passengers became ill.

    Recent findings suggest that the illnesses onboard were so bad that a “MANV 25” response was triggered at Frankfurt Airport. That’s a German emergency response alert for a mass casualty incident — “Massenanfall von Verletzten” (though fortunately there were no fatalities here).

    Passengers onboard were screened by medical teams, and one person on each flight was taken to a local hospital, while others are being monitored.

    Sources indicate that it’s not uncommon to hear stories of multiple people becoming sick on flights. Sometimes it’s a fume event, sometimes it could be a case of food poisoning (though it doesn’t usually happen that fast), etc. So what’s going on here, that people on two separate Condor flights became ill?

    Well, the passengers on these two flights had one thing in common — they all came off the AidaBella cruise ship in La Romana, and then these flights were sold as part of the cruise package.

    So while this is still being investigated, a norovirus outbreak on the cruise ship is believed to be the likely culprit. I’ve gotta say, an airplane seems like a pretty unpleasant place to come down with a gastrointestinal illness, so I imagine the lavatory situation onboard probably wasn’t great.

    Dozens of passengers on two separate Condor flights between the Dominican Republic and Germany around the same time became ill, triggering an emergency response at Frankfurt Airport, which included a couple of people being hospitalized.

    While it remains to be seen what caused this, the belief is that it could be some sort of a norovirus outbreak, based on the symptoms, as well as the fact that the passengers had all come off the same cruise ship. I hope everyone makes a quick recovery.

    What do you make of this Condor incident?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, in the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR, which will be the carrier’s first narrow body aircraft featuring latest generation interiors, including flat beds.
    • According to recent reports, qatar Airways at the moment has a total of 50 factory fresh Airbus A321-family aircraft on order.
    • Industry observers note that the expectation is that the first A321LR will be delivered in the coming weeks, before the end of 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, in the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR, which will be the carrier’s first narrow body aircraft featuring latest generation interiors, including flat beds. The airline will be introducing a “mini-Qsuite” type product on these planes, and we’ve now learned exactly when this new premium narrow body jet will enter service.

    According to recent reports, qatar Airways at the moment has a total of 50 factory fresh Airbus A321-family aircraft on order. This includes 10 A321LRs and 40 A321neos — both of those are latest generation aircraft, with the A321LR featuring additional range.

    Industry observers note that the expectation is that the first A321LR will be delivered in the coming weeks, before the end of 2026. The 10 A321LRs should join the fleet pretty quickly, and will then be followed by the A321neos. The A321LRs will be configured with 160 seats, including 16 business class seats and 144 economy class seats.

    In a recent development, the A321LR has a maximum range of 4,000 nautical miles, so it can be used for many destinations in Europe, Africa, and Asia. Below is a map showing the rough range from Doha (though in reality it won’t be quite as far, accounting for winds, fuel reserves, etc.).

    Now, for those paying close attention, I should acknowledge that Qatar Airways briefly flew six leased, all-economy A321neos, but those were just intended as a temporary solution, and are now flying for Sun PhuQuoc Airways, which is running an interesting operation.

    Qatar Airways’ A321neo-family aircraft order goes back a long time, and involved a lot of drama. The order was first declared in 2011, then the airline reconfirmed and upsized it in 2017. However, then former Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker got into a fight with Airbus over A350 production quality, and refused to take delivery of any Airbus planes.

    According to recent reports, that turned into a massive court battle, which was eventually resolved. But in the process, Qatar Airways lost all of its Airbus delivery slots, which is why these planes are coming way later than initially expected.

    Recent findings suggest that qatar Airways has been promising all along that it would introduce some sort of a next generation flat bed business class product on its Airbus A321LRs. As you’d expect, business class seats on narrow bodies sometimes differ from those on wide bodies, due to differing cabin constraints.

    What can we expect onboard these Qatar Airways A321LRs in business class? Executive Traveller quotes Qatar Airways CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater as saying that the new business class product will be based on the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform.

    Sources indicate that these planes will boast 16 business class seats, in a 1-1 configuration. This product offers reverse herringbone seats, and Qatar Airways plans to have doors at each seat as well, of course with its customized finishes.

    The launch customer for the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform was Air France on its A350s. However, that’s the wide body version of the seat, which is modified from the narrow body version.

    When it comes to the narrow body version of the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, ITA Airways was the launch customer, on its A321neos.

    This is also the product that Etihad is installing on its A321LRs. ITA Airways and Etihad don’t have doors in business class, but Qatar Airways does plan to offer it. Etihad also markets the first row of the cabin as first class (and that has doors), but I wouldn’t expect Qatar Airways to do something similar.

    This is about as good as narrow body business class seats get, as it’s generally preferred to the herringbone seats you’ll find on other carriers, like JetBlue A321LRs, American A321XLRs, etc.

    Qatar Airways now seems pretty certain about the delivery of its upcoming Airbus A321LRs, as the airline has officially put the first routes on sale, as flagged by AeroRoutes:.

    When you pull up the above flights, you’ll now see the seat map for the A321LR, which confirms the 16-seat business class cabin.

    In the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first of 10 Airbus A321LRs. This will be the first custom designed next generation narrow body that the airline takes delivery of. We knew the airline would offer flat bed seats on these planes, and now we have the details of that.

    The airline has gone with the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, the same product you’ll find on similar planes of Etihad and ITA Airways. However, unlike those airlines, Qatar Airways will have doors in business class. The planes will enter service by very early 2027, flying from Doha to both Vienna and Zurich.

    American Blocking Domestic Saver Awards Close To Departure (Within Six Days)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In May 2026, we saw American introduce a major upcoming restriction for award travel, which had the biggest implications for those redeeming on American through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club (in other words, anyone redeeming through a program other than American AAdvantage).
    • With this, American started to restrict its own saver level award availability close to departure.
    • Recent findings suggest that historically, American has been by far the best of the “major three” US carriers when it comes to making award seats on its own flights available, especially on domestic and short haul international flights.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In May 2026, we saw American introduce a major upcoming restriction for award travel, which had the biggest implications for those redeeming on American through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club (in other words, anyone redeeming through a program other than American AAdvantage).

    With this, American started to restrict its own saver level award availability close to departure. Initially, all domestic nonstop saver awards within six days of departure were pulled. In recent days, it looks like American has expanded this to all domestic connecting itineraries as well, so I’d like to cover those details (thanks to azbobcat for flagging this).

    Recent findings suggest that historically, American has been by far the best of the “major three” US carriers when it comes to making award seats on its own flights available, especially on domestic and short haul international flights. American actually releases a good amount of saver award seats across cabins, and it’s one of the things that makes AAdvantage better than the competition.

    However, in May 2026, we saw American introduce a major change to how it releases award space to partner frequent flyer programs. Long story short, American started blocking all nonstop, domestic saver award availability, for flights within six days (exactly 144 hours) of departure.

    As soon as a flight gets to the point where it’s 144 hours until departure, you’ll see that the airline “turns off” its saver fare classes — I’m referring specifically to the “U” (saver business class award) and “T” (saver economy award) fare classes, which show up when searching on ExpertFlyer, for example.

    Initially, this applied exclusively to nonstop, domestic award tickets, as connecting itineraries and all international itineraries (including short haul international ones) weren’t impacted by this. However, this seems to have now expanded to domestic connecting itineraries as well.

    Sources indicate that so any wholly domestic itinerary exclusively on American is no longer bookable at the saver level within six days of departure. International itineraries continue to be bookable within six days of departure, whether traveling nonstop or with a connection.

    What would cause American to suddenly “shut off” saver awards for domestic routes within days of departure?

    In a recent development, what’s interesting here is that the implications for AAdvantage members are limited. Yes, American has shut off awards in the saver fare classes, but that’s not to say that American isn’t making reasonably priced awards available within days of departure. American has long used some kind of dynamic award pricing concept for its own flights, regardless of whether or not there’s saver availability.

    It’s just that any awards in the official saver fare buckets aren’t available, and therefore aren’t bookable with points belonging to partner programs.

    It has been revealed that so it sure seems to me that the intent here is to block award availability for those booking through partner programs, like Alaska Atmos Rewards or British Airways Club. It goes without saying that I absolutely hate this restriction, as someone who “funds” a vast majority of my domestic American travel using Atmos Rewards points. At the same time, I also have to say that I can’t blame American for this change, as the airline has just made it too easy.

    I’ve been booking basically all my travel directly into American first class using Atmos Rewards points — I just set ExpertFlyer availability alerts for “U” class, it opens up a vast majority of the time, and then I book. It’s not surprising that American finally got a bit savvier.

    According to recent reports, american is now blocking all saver awards within exactly six days of departure for all domestic itineraries. This means within that timeframe, there’s no “U” or “T” availability, which corresponds to the saver business and economy award fare buckets, respectively. Initially this only applied to nonstop flights, while now it also applies to connecting itineraries.

    It has been revealed that for American AAdvantage members, the implications are limited, since American can still make reasonably priced awards available, just not formally in those fare buckets. The practical implications here are that partner programs just don’t have access to these award seats close to departure anymore.

    What do you make of American’s six day rule on award tickets?
